# Keys you hand over - qa-requirements-tester

## Outputs

- `work/requirements-register.md` - the register is the role's judgement; claim_projector.py copies the S3 planner's claims into it (a Register row, the ids entry and a `## Behaviour claims` row with origin S3-grounding) because the planner has no Bash and is not its writer: no role is added
- `work/requirements-readiness.json` - the same dispatch writes both; question_register.py adds a raised before/now question (`--raise`, the S4 exit, the S3 claim projector) under its answers lock
- `understanding.md` - the brief the person reads at gate A

Required at your stop (stage S2): `work/requirements-register.md`, `work/requirements-readiness.json`, `understanding.md`.
Re-run by the gate at your stop: `sizing.py` (advice only), `branch_accounting.py`.
The gate also reads:
- a derived requirement for each production module the diff creates: `derived`

## Witness

Your witness artifact (stages.json `witness`): `work/requirements-readiness.json`.

## Handoff form

Contract `s2-tester-to-strategist` (fill `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml`; `handoff_check.py` reads it):

- `inputs_read[].handed` (required) - the scout's `implementation.diff.hunks`
- `inputs_read[].read` (required) - how many hunks were actually opened
- `inputs_read[].version` (required) - the bundle revision or hash
- `header.window` (required) - TICKET
- `header.verdict` (required) - one of vocabulary.header_verdicts
- `scope[].id` (required) - R-n
- `scope[].state` (required) - one of vocabulary.row_states
- `scope[].reason` (required) - a verdict of at most 80 characters - the explanation lives in the artifact
- `scope[].kind` (required) - one of vocabulary.requirement_kinds - confirmed_ac|technical_invariant|derived_risk
- `scope[].source` (required) - SRC-ID or path, plus the revision it was read at
- `scope[].observable` (optional) - how it can be observed, or `none` with the reason
- `scope[].impact_class` (required) - the damage class, carried to the plan as impact_class
- `scope[].delta` (optional) - the register's delta column, new, changed or unchanged - optional; leave it out when the register has no such column
- `scope[].derived_from_hunk` (required) - path:line of the diff hunk, for a derived requirement; a dash otherwise
- `contradiction_matrix[].id` (required) - C-n
- `contradiction_matrix[].requirement` (required) - R-n
- `contradiction_matrix[].contradicts` (optional) - R-m, or the source and what it says
- `contradiction_matrix[].reading_a` (required) - what follows if the requirement stands
- `contradiction_matrix[].reading_b` (required) - what follows if the other side stands
- `contradiction_matrix[].owner_role` (required) - one of vocabulary.question_owners - po_ba|dev_arch|qa
- `open_questions[].id` (required) - Q-n
- `open_questions[].statement` (required) - the question, one sentence
- `open_questions[].owner_role` (required) - one of vocabulary.question_owners - po_ba|dev_arch|qa
- `open_questions[].severity` (required) - blocking|non_blocking
- `open_questions[].sources_say` (required) - what the sources say, with where
- `open_questions[].readings[].reading` (required) - what it would mean
- `open_questions[].readings[].cost` (required) - what testing it this way costs or risks
- `size.computed` (required) - one of vocabulary.sizes - XS|S|M|L|XL|XXL
- `size.override` (optional) - the role's override, or a dash
- `claims.every_hunk_of_the_diff_was_read` (required) - true|false
- `claims.every_requirement_has_an_observable_or_says_none` (required) - true|false
- `claims.contradiction_matrix_walked_in_full` (required) - true|false
- `claims.size_computed_by_sizing_py_not_quoted` (required) - true|false
- `claims.size_recorded_in_pipeline` (required) - true|false
- `tried[].requirement` (required) - R-n, a source id or an area
- `tried[].technique` (required) - the technique by its name in your charter
- `tried[].observation` (required) - what you saw, in one line
- `tried[].evidence` (required) - the path (and anchor) where it shows
- `tried_note` (optional) - why the table is empty, or a dash when it has rows
- `unresolved[].id` (required) - R-n or Q-n
- `unresolved[].reason` (required) - one of vocabulary.unresolved_reasons
- `unresolved[].detail` (required) - what exactly is missing, and what would settle it
- `blocked.field` (only when blocked) - the field of this file the role cannot fill
- `blocked.problem` (only when blocked) - what the role tried and what refused it, verbatim
- `blocked.tried[]` (only when blocked) - command or step, and its answer
- `blocked.data[]` (only when blocked) - path of anything the conductor needs to see

Every handoff form shares one skeleton (`common_shape` of handoffs/index.yaml): `inputs`, `inputs_read`, `header`, `scope`, `artifacts`, `claims`, `unresolved`, `blocked`.

## What code will check of you

`<T>` is your ticket, `<ID>` your dispatch id, `<home>` the project's qa-factory folder - all three stand in your prompt (`Ticket: ... Dispatch: ...`) and in your task packet.

- [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] Your final message is the handoff form: a header `<role> <stage> <window> · ok|concerns|halt|impossible`; one line `<id> · <state> · <reason of at most 80 characters>` for every item of the dispatch's scope (a halting digest owes no scope lines); nothing but those lines between the header and the path; and, last, the task-relative path of what you wrote (a halting digest may omit it). A verdict or a state word outside the form's list is advice, not a refusal; a reason over 80 characters, an absolute path under the task root, prose before the header and a missing path the witness names are mended by code when mending makes the form pass. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [exit_gate:EG-text-end] Your dispatch ends with the host's handback tool carrying your digest line, never with free text after it. Door: call the host's handback tool with your digest line.
- [handoff_check:blocked_problem] A row in state `blocked` carries `blocked.problem`; `blocked_by_env` is used only where `options_for_role` offers it to this role. Door: write the problem, or pick a state the role is offered.
- [handoff_check:claims] What the form claims is true is true on disk ("the form claims this is true, and it is not"). Door: fix the claim or make it true.
- [handoff_check:cli] The call names an existing UTF-8 form with a `contract:` line and an existing values file; `--shorten` only with `--fix`. Door: the refusal's door; a non-UTF-8 form: run `handoff_init` again.
- [handoff_check:field.blank] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: write the value as a `path: value` line in the values file, then run the check again.
- [handoff_check:field.max_len] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: shorten it (`--shorten` with `--fix`) or rewrite.
- [handoff_check:field.value] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: write one of the listed words (or `new: <word> -- <why>` where the list is open).
- [handoff_check:findings_tooling] A finding whose cause is `tooling` is repeated in `tooling_findings`. Door: add it to `tooling_findings`.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.failures] Each shown failure has a triage row. Door: triage it once.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.listing] Everything named in `listed_in` exists, and nothing extra stands. Door: list exactly what exists.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.names] Every row has a name. Door: name the row.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.repairs] No repair is pending when the null outcome is claimed. Door: finish or record the repair.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.report] The run report is readable. Door: rerun / point at the readable report.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.verdict] The triage verdict is a known word. Door: write a known verdict.
- [handoff_check:required_rows] A required list has one row per item in scope: the id, a state and a reason of at most 80 characters. Door: write the rows as index lines in the values file, then run this check again.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.null_word] A list's null-outcome word (the declared empty outcome) stands only when the list has no rows; never both. Door: remove the word or remove the rows.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.owed_by_verdict] When the verdict owes rows (the verdict word names work done on items), the list is not empty. Door: write the rows the verdict owes, or change the verdict.
- [handoff_check:tried] In a contract that asks what was tried (TRIED_CONTRACTS), each tried entry states what was tried and the error it gave (TRIED_MEANING). Door: fill the tried entry with the attempt and its error.
- [handoff_check:values_apply] Each path names a field of this contract, by its index where it is a list row, not a contract-owned path; a list field gets a list and a one-value field one value; rows open in order. Door: correct the path (the refusal suggests "did you mean").
- [handoff_check:values_file] The values file is `path: value` lines (or a JSON object): valid JSON, an object not a list, each path given once, each key a field path, no nested value. Door: fix the line the refusal names (FILE_FIX).
- [exit_gate:digest] Your final message has the digest form stated in the row [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] of this section. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [validate_artifacts:check_behaviour_claims] Every requirement seen only in the implementation has exactly one entry under the behaviour-claims heading, with an `origin` from its list and the fields of a claim. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_cell_counts] A table row never holds more cells than its header; a bar inside a cell is written as `|`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_delta_column] With a `delta` column, every row carries `new`, `changed` or `unchanged`, and an `unchanged` row does not cite the diff as its observable. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_manifest_reuse] Every path the register cites was recorded in the S1 context manifest. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_register] The register's front matter carries the required fields, non-empty `ids` of the form R-n, sources from the source list and `confidence` high or low; every declared id has a full-width row under the register heading with a listed source (or a derivation), matrix cells per the grammar and an impact from the project's scale. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_requirements_review] `requirements-review.md` carries the required front matter, a `mode` and a `verdict` from their lists, and in mode B the matrix fields. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_understanding] The understanding file stays within `UNDERSTANDING_MAX_LINES`, has every section of `UNDERSTANDING_SECTIONS`, and names every requirement id in a "What we verify" or "What we do not verify" line. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [guard_pre_tool:*] 23 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [stage_guard:*] 8 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
